settings.agents.codex.binaryPath.descrip: Absolute path to the `codex` binary. Leave empty to auto-discover via PATH.
settings.agents.copilot.binaryPath.descr: Absolute path to the GitHub Copilot CLI binary. Leave empty to auto-discover via PATH.
settings.agents.claude.binaryPath.descri: Absolute path to the `claude` binary. Leave empty to auto-discover via PATH.
settings.agents.codex.permissionMode.des: Default permission tier for @codex: how much it asks before running commands or changing files. Override for a single turn with `/ask`, `/acceptEdits` or `/fullAuto`.
settings.agents.copilot.permissionMode.d: Default permission tier for @copilot-cli: how much it asks before running commands or changing files. Override for a single turn with `/ask`, `/acceptEdits` or `/fullAuto`.
settings.agents.claude.permissionMode.de: Default permission tier for @claude: how much it asks before running commands or changing files. Override for a single turn with `/ask`, `/acceptEdits` or `/fullAuto`.
settings.agents.codex.maxApiCallsPerTurn: Maximum number of model API calls Codex may make within a single turn before it's force-interrupted. Guards against a runaway loop (e.g. the model repeatedly calling tools without converging) that would otherwise never reach `turn/completed`.
settings.agents.copilot.maxApiCallsPerTu: Maximum number of model API calls the Copilot CLI may make within a single turn before it's force-aborted. Guards against a runaway loop (e.g. the model repeatedly calling tools without converging) that would otherwise never reach `session.idle`.
settings.agents.claude.maxApiCallsPerTur: Maximum number of model round-trips the Claude Agent SDK may make within a single turn (its own `maxTurns` option). Guards against a runaway loop (e.g. the model repeatedly calling tools without converging); past this, the SDK ends the turn itself instead of running unbounded.
settings.agents.codex.shareMcpServers.de: Pass MCP servers from VS Code's own native mcp.json config (user profile + every workspace folder's `.vscode/mcp.json`) down to @codex. Disable if you only want @codex's own separately configured MCP servers (e.g. via `codex mcp add`).
Pass MCP servers from VS Code's own native mcp.json config (user profile + every workspace folder's `.vscode/mcp.json`) down to @copilot-cli. Disable if you only want the Copilot CLI's own separately configured MCP servers.
settings.agents.claude.shareMcpServers.d: Pass MCP servers from VS Code's own native mcp.json config (user profile + every workspace folder's `.vscode/mcp.json`) down to @claude, letting the Claude Agent SDK connect to them itself. **Defaults to off**, because the Claude Agent SDK's own MCP client can't complete OAuth — servers that need it (e.g. Atlassian) silently fail to connect. Instead, by default those servers are managed by VS Code (which does support OAuth) and their tools are exposed to @claude through the dynamic-tool bridge, see `#feima.agents.claude.tools.excludePatterns#`. Enable this only for MCP servers you want @claude's own SDK to connect to directly.
settings.agents.codex.systemPrompt.descr: Extra instructions for @codex, layered on top of Codex's own built-in agent instructions as `developerInstructions`. There is no additional Feima-provided default — this setting is purely for your own customization. See `#feima.agents.codex.systemPromptMode#`.
settings.agents.copilot.systemPrompt.des: Extra instructions for @copilot-cli. There is no additional Feima-provided default — this setting is purely for your own customization. See `#feima.agents.copilot.systemPromptMode#` for how it's applied.
settings.agents.claude.systemPrompt.desc: Extra instructions for @claude, on top of Claude Code's own default persona/instructions and Feima's built-in VS Code context notes. See `#feima.agents.claude.systemPromptMode#` for how this combines with those defaults.
settings.agents.codex.systemPromptMode.d: How `#feima.agents.codex.systemPrompt#` is applied for @codex. Currently equivalent either way — see enum descriptions.
settings.agents.copilot.systemPromptMode: How `#feima.agents.copilot.systemPrompt#` combines with the Copilot CLI's own default system message.
How `#feima.agents.claude.systemPrompt#` combines with the built-in defaults for @claude.
settings.agents.tools.excludePatterns.de: Tool names (from `vscode.lm.tools`) to hide from the dynamic-tool bridge shared by agent participants. Supports a single `*` wildcard per pattern. The default excludes MCP-backed tools (`mcp_*` — MCP servers are handled natively by each CLI's own MCP client, see `.vscode/mcp.json`), a few Copilot Chat manifest-only tools with no runtime implementation, and internal agent-loop control signals from other agent SDKs.
settings.agents.codex.tools.excludePatte: Overrides `#feima.agents.tools.excludePatterns#` for @codex only. Leave unset to use the shared list; set to an array (including `[]`) to replace it just for @codex.
settings.agents.copilot.tools.excludePat: Overrides `#feima.agents.tools.excludePatterns#` for @copilot-cli only. Leave unset to use the shared list; set to an array (including `[]`) to replace it just for @copilot-cli.
settings.agents.claude.tools.excludePatt: Overrides `#feima.agents.tools.excludePatterns#` for @claude only. **Defaults to the shared list minus `mcp_*`**, so VS Code-managed MCP tools (including OAuth-authenticated ones the Claude SDK can't reach on its own, see `#feima.agents.claude.shareMcpServers#`) are exposed to @claude via the dynamic-tool bridge. Set to an empty array `[]` to disable all exclusions for @claude, or a custom array to replace the default.
chatCommand.permission.ask.description: Ask for approval before every tool action, for this turn only
chatCommand.permission.acceptEdits.descr: Auto-approve file edits and ask for the rest, for this turn only
chatCommand.permission.fullAuto.descript: Auto-approve everything and never ask, for this turn only
